subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the Windows CI lane add recurring native PowerShell smoke coverage for `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke`, or should that command set be narrowed until the docs command is Windows-safe?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding recurring commands to the narrower Windows runner pool and sequencing around the blocked docs command needs maintainer CI-scope intent.

options.title: Land focused smoke after proof
options.body: Accept the Windows runner cost once the selected commands pass under native `pwsh` and the linked PR includes redacted after-fix proof.

options.title: Narrow the first smoke
options.body: Start with only commands that already pass under native `pwsh` and keep the docs command covered by the separate docs-script repair path.

options.title: Defer CI expansion
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause the PR until maintainers decide the Windows runner budget should absorb this recurring smoke.

recommendation.title: Land focused smoke after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the Windows runner cost once the selected commands pass under native `pwsh` and the linked PR includes redacted after-fix proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and docs history put the Windows CI lane and runner-scope guidance closest to this owner path.
